chunk_findings.detail: The AST check iterates only `ast.parse(harness.read_text("utf-8")).body`, so it inspects only top-level import statements. If `ddflow/services/approvals/harness.py` has (or later gains) an `import urllib`, `import http`, or `import socket` nested inside a function, `if TYPE_CHECKING:`, `try:`, or other block, `roots` stays empty and the assertion passes. `importlinter` scans nested nodes, so `test_import_contracts` would still fail; this regression test therefore does not actually guard the contract against the drift it claims to prevent.

chunk_findings.detail: The import scan only walks `ast.parse(...).body`, so it never sees imports nested in functions, classes, or `if` blocks. Given `harness.py` whose only network import is `def load(): import urllib.request` (or the same under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`), `roots` stays empty, the intersection assert passes, and the baseline assert also passes if no ignore line was added. That is the bug class this regression claims to lock: the module still imports `urllib`, while `test_harness_imports_no_http_roots_and_holds_no_http_home_entry` stays green.

evidence.note: Claim: bug_fixed marks a bug fixed while its own fix task is still working unmerged. Mechanism: _verify_regression's worktree branch runs the regression test on base vs worktree and records verified for an unlanded fix task; nothing checks the branch landed. Refutation: close a bug whose own fix task is claimed but unmerged; observe exit 0 regression_verified=verified. chunk_findings.detail: The patch deletes the regression test for bug B2e5ca93520 and its setup helper. That test specifically created an unknown-author repository with a same-family deepseek reviewer listed first and asserted the identifying reviewer is one of the cross-family reviewers (xai/google). With this deletion and no replacement in the manifest, the exact bug scenario is no longer checked: if `api.review(repo, gate="critic", item="T1", branch="feat")` again selects the first same-family reviewer for an unknown author, CI will stay green. Because `ddflow/api/review/run.py` is also modified in this change, dropping the only regression guard for this reviewer-independence invariant is a defect.

chunk_findings.detail: The change replaces `_case(repo)` with `_merge(repo)`, but `_merge` does not create B1 or its `fix-B1` task; it assumes `_case` has already run. On a fresh `repo` fixture there is no `fix-B1` task, so `run_cli(repo, "merge", "fix-B1")` inside `_merge` fails and the test errors out before reaching `api.bug_fixed`, meaning the intended verification behavior is never exercised.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `fix-not-landed` refusal is computed in `_regression_verdict` solely from `_owns_unlanded_fix(fx, rec)` and never checks the `landing` value, even though `_unlanded_fix_source` explicitly advertises `--landed <sha>` as an accepted way to close the bug. Concrete input: bug `B` has `rec.fix_task = "fix-1"`, `fx` is `fix-1` with `fx.merged_sha == None`, and the user runs `ddflow bug fixed B --regression-test <test> --landed <sha>` where `<sha>` is a valid landed commit containing the fix. The command reaches line 565 and returns `"fix-not-landed"`, causing the caller to return `O.refused(...)` at the new line 201, even though the user supplied the landed commit the remedy told them to supply. The guard must treat an explicit `landing` as landed regardless of the worktree task’s `merged_sha`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge/bug_close.py:565

chunk_findings.detail: The new close gate treats “not landed” as `not fx.merged_sha` only, then the remedy in `_unlanded_fix_source` tells the operator to recover with `bug fixed --landed <sha>`. That flag is never consulted: the check at the post-verify return (`verdict in ("verified", "verified-by-mutation") and _owns_unlanded_fix(fx, rec)`) does not take the `landing` pair, and the `fix-not-landed` refusal runs even when `landing` is already set. Given a fix commit that is on the base (or named with `--landed <sha>`) while the fix-task record still has an empty `merged_sha`, regression verification can pass and the close is still refused with instructions that repeat the same failing command.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `fix-not-landed` refusal is computed in `_regression_verdict` solely from `_owns_unlanded_fix(fx, rec)` and never checks the `landing` value, even though `_unlanded_fix_source` explicitly advertises `--landed <sha>` as an accepted way to close the bug. Concrete input: bug `B` has `rec.fix_task = "fix-1"`, `fx` is `fix-1` with `fx.merged_sha == None`, and the user runs `ddflow bug fixed B --regression-test <test> --landed <sha>` where `<sha>` is a valid landed commit containing the fix. The command reaches line 565 and returns `"fix-not-landed"`, causing the caller to return `O.refused(...)` at the new line 201, even though the user supplied the landed commit the remedy told them to supply. The guard must treat an explicit `landing` as landed regardless of the worktree task’s `merged_sha`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge/bug_close.py:565

chunk_findings.detail: The new close gate treats “not landed” as `not fx.merged_sha` only, then the remedy in `_unlanded_fix_source` tells the operator to recover with `bug fixed --landed <sha>`. That flag is never consulted: the check at the post-verify return (`verdict in ("verified", "verified-by-mutation") and _owns_unlanded_fix(fx, rec)`) does not take the `landing` pair, and the `fix-not-landed` refusal runs even when `landing` is already set. Given a fix commit that is on the base (or named with `--landed <sha>`) while the fix-task record still has an empty `merged_sha`, regression verification can pass and the close is still refused with instructions that repeat the same failing command.

data.summary: lan-deepseek-v4-pro (deepseek = author family, local, 600-800s/chunk) never produces a clean delta round across 11 rounds, so rubber_duck/critic stay "confirmed finding with no later delta that re-raised them" and ddflow refuses merge -- even though gemini/google and grok/xai (cross-family) both passed 0 findings and kimi was 429/unavailable. The rule "the authors own model never counts" + cross-family-clean should let the cross-family clean verdict close the gate; instead the non-converging same-family reviewer blocks every remaining item. Root cause: reviewer verdict aggregation treats a same-family reviewers confirmed-then-unconverged findings as merge-blocking rather than discounted when a cross-family reviewer passed clean.
data.title: a same-family reviewer that never converges blocks merge even when cross-family reviewers pass clean

chunk_findings.detail: The new refusal remedy instructs the user to run `ddflow complete {named} --regression-test`. This is an incomplete command: `--regression-test` requires a `<test>` argument, as the change's own intent shows (`ddflow complete fix-... --regression-test <test>`). A user who follows the suggested command literally gets a CLI argument-parsing error instead of a closable command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge/bug_close.py:_unlanded_fix_source

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds `_merge` to the surrounding regression-verdict tests but misses the test that ends at line 127 with `assert out.data["regression_verified"] == "could-not-run", out.data`. That test is set up via `_case(repo)`, which leaves `fix-B1` unmerged. After the new fix-not-landed gate, `api.bug_fixed` with no `--landed` now returns the `fix-not-landed` refusal before the regression runner is reached, so `out.data["regression_verified"]` is not `could-not-run` and the assertion fails. Running this test after the change will fail, so the change does not pass its own test suite; the test should call `_merge(repo)` before `api.bug_fixed` like the adjacent tests.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_bug_regression_verified.py:127

chunk_findings.detail: In `test_an_unrecognized_verification_status_is_recorded_not_verified`, the comment says `set up B1 + fix-B1, then land it so the close reaches the patch`, but because `_merge(repo)` is called after `_case(repo)`, the close actually executes against the landed state (where `fx.merged_sha` is present and `_owns_unlanded_fix` returns `False`), which avoids the new `fix-not-landed` verdict rather than testing the unmerged patch path that the comment implies.
